t: Determine the Winner of a Bowling Game — Score Simulation
o: A turn counts double if either of the player's previous two turns was a strike (10 pins). Compute each player's score independently and compare. Example 1: player 1 gets 5 + 10 + 2·3 + 2·2 = 25 vs 21 → 1. Example 4 shows strikes keep doubling subsequent turns while the streak lasts. n ≤ 1000 makes a direct simulation ideal.
k: Doubling depends only on the same player's prior two turns — evaluate each array independently.
Condition for turn i: player[i-1] == 10 or (i ≥ 2 and player[i-2] == 10).

a.i: For each turn add x or 2x according to whether the previous one or two turns were strikes; then compare totals.
s: Write a score(p) helper implementing the doubling rule.

w: Straightforward; the only trap is boundary checks for i−1/i−2 and remembering that a strike two turns back still doubles the current turn. Follow-up: real bowling scoring with frames/spares, or processing turns online as a stream.
